changes: Use the term Frontier Wars, as the NSW syllabus does, alongside or in place of frontier conflict.
State that the conflicts were over water and food as well as land.

match.reason: The bank card covers the same frontier conflict and resistance idea, but it is written for Year 9 and uses a different term, and it does not mention water and food or the whole period across every colony, so it needs small changes rather than being reused as it is.

confirm.reason: The bank point covers forms of First Nations resistance, named resistance leaders and the Myall Creek massacre, while the new point is the broader overview of the Frontier Wars as a long period of conflict over land, water and food across every colony, so the bank card teaches a different focus rather than the same idea.

draft.title: The Frontier Wars
card: As British colonists spread out from the first settlements, they took up land for farms and grazing. This land was already the Country of Aboriginal Peoples.
Colonists also used the waterholes, rivers and hunting grounds that Aboriginal people relied on for water and food. Conflict over land, water and food followed.
This conflict broke out in every colony and went on for a long time. The long period of violence is now called the Frontier Wars.
Aboriginal people defended their Country in many ways. Many Aboriginal people were killed, and colonists died too.
draft.remember: Frontier Wars: as colonists spread, conflict over land, water and food broke out in every colony.

a.q: Why did conflict break out as colonists spread across Australia?
opts: Colonists took land and water that Aboriginal people used
Aboriginal people moved onto farms colonists had left empty
Colonists and Aboriginal people argued over British money
Aboriginal people asked to join colonial towns and were refused
a.why: Colonists took up land and used waterholes and hunting grounds that Aboriginal people depended on, which led to conflict. The option about empty farms is wrong because the land was already Aboriginal Country, so colonists were the ones moving onto it.
a.clue: Think about what colonists needed and who already used it.

b.q: Which statement about the Frontier Wars is correct?
opts: They were conflicts in every colony over a long period
They were a single battle fought in one colony
They were fought only in the first years after 1788
They were fought only between British soldiers and convicts
b.why: The conflicts broke out in every colony and went on for a long time, which is why they are called a series of wars. A single battle is the tempting mistake, but the violence was widespread and lasted well beyond the first years.
b.clue: The name is plural, and the card says where and how long.
